rationale:
WHY THIS CHANGE EXISTS, and why the obvious version of it would have been WORSE than doing nothing.

bugs_open/469. `check_section_source_drift` detects that a page's section list disagrees between the authoritative store (site_plan_sections, else the site_specs.site_plan aspect) and pages.sections, and files a flag-only work item saying "the next build will overwrite the cache". It has never been able to close one. Three properties compounded: nothing closed the items so they accumulated (six open, the oldest 37 days); the item's spec is frozen at filing time and reads as CURRENT; and an OPEN item suppresses re-filing, because idx_swi_dedup is UNIQUE (site_id, item_key) over non-terminal statuses — so the detector went blind on exactly the pages it had already flagged. On robot-hands.com/gripper-catalog that ran for 37 days and a section a human had deliberately added (migration SQL_2026-07-24_r9, an owner-backed call) was destroyed. It is the same component migration 154 was written to rescue in July.

THE SHARP EDGE, which is the whole design. For this check, "the finding no longer reproduces" and "the damage completed" are THE SAME OBSERVATION: the stores agree again precisely BECAUSE the build synced the authority down over the cache. So the obvious closer — retract when the stores agree — would close, automatically and fleet-wide, exactly the cases that most need a human. It would convert a silence into a certificate. That is strictly worse than today.

WHY `lost` AND NOT `direction` IS THE TEST. Migration 753 ran this classification by hand on 2026-09-03 with a three-way equality (cache_held / authority_won / third_list). That label cannot separate two cases with opposite meanings, and both are in the real backlog: on oufe.com/contact the authority RESTORED a section the cache had dropped (authority_won, nothing destroyed); on robot-hands.com/gripper-catalog the authority DELETED one (authority_won, a live section gone). So the receipt fires on a computed LOSS — names the frozen cache held that the frozen authority did not, minus what is on the page today — while `direction` is still recorded on every close, byte-compatible with 753, because LANDMINES tells readers to query result->>'direction'.

WHY THE COUPLING LIVES ON THE SHARED SEAM AND NOT IN THE CHECK. The owner's 2026-08-02 ruling is that new authority on a shared seam ships as an opt-in field with the unsafe default OFF, not as a rule in a doc comment, because "a comment is not a control on a tree this many sessions share". resolveWorkItems has TWO callers today (discovery_checks.go:274 and work_item_retraction.go:230); a control placed in either one protects only that one. ResolvedFinding.Receipt is nil for every existing check, so their behaviour is byte-identical — including the six-argument UPDATE their tests assert, which is why the evidence argument is appended CONDITIONALLY rather than always-with-NULL.

SCOPE POSITION, stated rather than assumed. This adds a field to a shared struct and a precondition inside a shared function. It changes no guarantee any existing caller relies on (nil = today), and it ADDS one for callers that opt in. Under the owner ruling of 2026-07-29 §1 that is the normal gate rather than architecture-scope, but the architecture seat should say so if it disagrees; I am not claiming the RFC_022 narrowing, because this change DOES have a live consumer naming it in the same commit.

WHAT I DELIBERATELY DID NOT DO. (1) No new pages.sections history table. I was one query from proposing one and it was refuted: migration 357's trigger pair already archives every deleted page_components row with slot_name, position and rendered_html — 24 rows for gripper-spec-sheet alone. The BYTES survive; the LIST does not, because every rebuild deletes every row, so the receipt copies the list and points at the archive for the bytes. (2) No writer to site_plan_sections — RFC_064 is open with the owner and belongs to the 427 lane; I coordinated the split with that session directly. (3) No refresh of the frozen spec, although refreshOnConflict exists: the frozen lists ARE the baseline `lost` is computed from, and refreshing them would erase the only surviving record of the destroyed composition. The dedup blindness is fixed by FREEING the slot instead. (4) No changes to the other nine flag-only checks with no closer; the seam is reusable, each predicate is its own.

FILES MENTIONED HERE THAT ARE NOT IN THE EDIT LIST, each with its reason. docs/agent_docs/sql_for_agents/760_..._HOLD.sql and its _ROLLBACK — the held robot-hands repair, committed separately, outside this task's coherent unit and not needed to review this code. bugs_open/469, docs024_key_docs_latest/bugfix_469_drift_closer/* and LANDMINES.md — prose, refused client-side by council scope, so listing them would spend the round without ever showing a reviewer the file; all are written and committed. docs026_concept_register/register/work-item-integrity.md — the register entry the 2026-07-28 ruling requires in the same commit as a new seam; also prose and also refused client-side, and it IS written and committed alongside this change rather than deferred.

EVIDENCE DISCIPLINE. Every safety property below was proven by MUTATION, not by a passing mock: 11 mutations of the check and 4 of the seam were each applied by script, observed to fail a named test, and the source restored and diffed byte-identical. One of the four SURVIVED on first run — deleting the receipt-insert error return left the test green because a second guard in series also refused — and the test was sharpened to discriminate rather than the survival being read as "the line is fine".

plan.summary: bugs_open/469: give check_section_source_drift a DIRECTION-AWARE closer that cannot ratify the loss it just observed, by making the record of a destroyed composition a precondition of the retraction on the shared seam.
plan.risks: The retraction pass adds two site-scoped reads (open items; live slot identities) to a check that already issues four, on a daily discovery sweep — bounded and cheap. The wide branch is unreachable: every retraction here is narrow (one page's key), never AllOfType. Two closes of the same page inside the anti-churn 7-day window could brand a third filing 'unresolved' (retractable, non-blocking; that is RFC_010 Q1, estate-wide, not this change). The receipt is another handler-less needs_human_review item in a queue the estate demonstrably does not drain (capability_gap: 331 items, 42 days) — the defence is only partial and stated: the safety property is not that the receipt is READ but that the close CANNOT HAPPEN WITHOUT IT, so a loss is never laundered into 'resolved'; the detection-time grade acts before the loss and shrinks the receipt population; and bugs_open/033 owns the drain. The name-based presence match over-grades to 'high' on a build_status='removed' row (1.7% of rows, the safe direction) and the spec key says would_drop_present rather than _deployed for exactly that reason.

edits.rationale: Two opt-in fields on the shared retraction seam, nil = exactly today's behaviour for all 19 checks that retract, plus RecurrenceExpected on WorkItemSpec so a receipt filed for a SECOND loss on the same page is not dropped by the anti-churn brake (the page_divergence_overwritten precedent). Receipt's doc comment carries the contract: a check may retract a finding whose resolution destroyed something ONLY by recording what was destroyed, in the same transaction.
edits.sketch:
type WorkItemSpec struct {
 	CreatedBy    string
 	ItemKey      string
 	BatchID      uuid.UUID
+	// Set when each finding is a NEW EVENT rather than a repeat of the same one.
+	RecurrenceExpected bool
 }

 type ResolvedFinding struct {
 	Reason string
+	// Receipt MUST be durably present before this retraction is applied.
+	// resolveWorkItems writes it first, in the SAME transaction, and REFUSES
+	// the retraction if it can neither insert it nor confirm an open one.
+	// Opt-in, unsafe default OFF (owner ruling 2026-08-02): nil is exactly
+	// today's behaviour, so no existing check is affected.
+	Receipt *WorkItemSpec
+	// Evidence merges into the closed row's `result` jsonb, so a machine close
+	// and migration 753's hand-written close record the same shape.
+	Evidence map[string]interface{}
 }

edits.rationale: The enforcement half, inside the ONE implementation both callers share. Receipt before close, same transaction, so a run that dies between them leaves the finding OPEN rather than the loss unrecorded. `!inserted` is CONFIRMED rather than assumed, because insertWorkItem returns false for several reasons and only one of them means a durable record exists — assuming it turns a dropped receipt into a silent close, which is the hole the field exists to fill. workItemFromSpec is extracted from the runner's inline literal because there are now two places a spec becomes a row and two hand-kept copies of one field mapping is the drift class this estate keeps paying for.

The runner's inline WorkItemSpec->workItem literal becomes the shared mapper, so the insert path and the receipt path cannot map a field differently. The retraction Warn gains receipt_required, because a receipt-bearing retraction that fails was WITHHELD on purpose and a reader must be able to tell that from ordinary bad luck in the logs.

edits.rationale: The consumer. THREE parts. (a) Detection-time grading: a multiset difference computes what the sync-down will DROP versus ADD, name-matched against live page_components slots; severity becomes high only when the drop is a name the page currently carries, and the summary leads with it. This is the only part that acts BEFORE the loss. It is a MULTISET difference because one live plan names generic-text-block six times and a set difference reports 'nothing dropped' when six become five. The spec key is would_drop_present, not _deployed, because the projection carries no build_status and the check has not measured deployment (removed rows are 56 of 3,333, an over-grade in the safe direction; slot_name is never NULL, 0 of 3,333, so the name match has no silent under-report). (b) The retraction pass, placed BEFORE the filing loop and before the per-pass cap — the recorded landmine is that a monotonic check's early return makes its retraction inert on exactly the zero-finding site whose stale items need closing. It never infers from absence: a page whose row has vanished yields no observation and its item stays open, and a 'no higher source names this page' close requires a DEMAND CONTROL that the authority read produced rows for some other page, because an empty read for the whole site is indistinguishable from a mid-replan window. Items are shape-graded, not producer-listed (the GradesFunc principle: any agent definition can file any item_type from DB config, so a code-side producer list is permanently behind live config). It carries NO status vocabulary, following findResolvedEmptySections' stated reason that this package already holds two disagreeing copies of that list and resolveWorkItems owns the predicate. (c) The receipt, built by the SAME function that computes the loss, so a lossy retraction cannot be obtained without it; a source-pin test asserts the file holds exactly one ResolvedFinding construction.

REQUIRED IN THE SAME COMMIT, and the guard enforces it: the source-scan sensor breaks the build on a new ItemType string it cannot classify. section_composition_lost is classified catJudgement with the reason it can never have a verifier — the only mechanical re-observation is 'the section is back', and its negation is equally 'the removal was intended and accepted', so a verifier would fail-closed on correctly-resolved items for ever. It is also added to liveItemTypes by the union rule (from the moment it is minted, not at the next hand-refresh), and section_source_drift's own note records that it is now self-clearing. Note the check file spells its item types as strings at the field sites rather than using its constants: the escape hatch (computedItemTypeSites) would have made BOTH types invisible to classification, a hole in the guard exactly where it claims coverage.

edits.rationale: The check's tests, headed by a MUTATION TABLE naming eleven mutations and the test each must kill. All eleven were applied by script, observed to fail, and the source restored and diffed byte-identical — a mock's own bookkeeping cannot assert a negative. The table-driven classifier test walks the real 2026-09-03 backlog, because the cases that matter are the two where `direction` and `lost` DISAGREE (oufe.com/contact: authority_won, nothing lost; gripper-catalog: authority_won, a live section gone). The locked-row case is the one that would have filed a false destruction receipt on every locked page on the estate had `lost` subtracted the raw cache instead of the merged list.

The seam's own tests, including the regression guard for OTHER lanes: a retraction with no Evidence must still send exactly the six arguments every existing caller's test asserts. Four mutations were run; the FIRST SURVIVED and that is recorded in the file rather than quietly fixed — deleting the receipt-insert error return left the test green because the flow fell through to the !inserted arm whose unmocked SELECT errors too, so a guard in SERIES did the work. The safety property held; the test's claim to pin that line did not. It now asserts the specific message.

grounded_in: registry.go CheckResult.Resolved: 'A retraction fires ONLY on a positive observation. Nothing anywhere derives "resolved" from an EMPTY Findings slice ... Deriving retraction from absence would quietly close real defects fleet-wide, which is a far worse failure than the one this fixes.'

bugs_open/469 §3: 'An open item SUPPRESSES re-filing. idx_swi_dedup is UNIQUE (site_id, item_key) over non-terminal statuses, so while a stale item sits open, genuinely new drift on that same page cannot be filed. The detector blinds itself on exactly the pages it has already flagged.'

bugs_open/469 §2 correction: 'The direction test correctly said "the authority won"; it cannot say whether what the authority won *with* was equivalent — which is precisely why `authority_won` must route to a human and never auto-close as resolved.'

Migration 753 receipt on robot-hands.com/gripper-catalog, read live 2026-09-03: result->>'direction' = 'authority_won', direction_note = 'THE CACHE WAS OVERWRITTEN — whatever was edited into pages.sections was destroyed by the tier-1 sync-down. Closed only so it stops blocking the detector; the loss itself is filed separately.'

load_page_sections_from_spec_action.go:558-570 — the sync: 'UPDATE pages SET sections = $1::jsonb ... WHERE site_id = $2 AND name = $3 AND sections IS DISTINCT FROM $1::jsonb'. No re-plan is required; any page BUILD does this.

check_empty_sections.go findResolvedEmptySections: 'There is no `status NOT IN (...)` filter here, and adding one would be a mistake worth naming. This package already holds TWO hand-rolled copies of that list and they ALREADY DISAGREE ... resolveWorkItems owns the predicate; this function owns the observation.'

check_archived_page_still_serving.go:410-414 — the landmine this change's pass ordering obeys: 'a monotonic check's `if len(findings) == 0 { return }` early return makes its new retraction INERT on exactly the sites that need it — the zero-findings site is the ONLY site the early return fires on, and it is precisely the site whose stale items need closing.'

verifiers.go GradesFunc: 'IT KEYS ON THE ROW, NEVER ON A PRODUCER LIST ... any agent definition can file any item_type from DB config with no code change, so such a list is authoritative-looking and permanently behind live config.'

page_component_divergence.go:219-222 — the RecurrenceExpected precedent: 'Each divergence is a new genuine event (a different patch was destroyed); without this the two-strike guard silently drops the third same-key finding.'

The BYTES survive a loss; the LIST does not, because DELETE+INSERT is the rebuild lifecycle (357 header: 19,054 deletes vs 4,928 updates).

[MEASURED 2026-09-03, live clients_db] page_components: 3,219 deployed / 56 removed / 32 pending / 26 approved, and slot_name is NULL on 0 of all 3,333 rows. So the name match under-reports never, and over-grades to `high` on at most 1.7% of rows.

All six section_source_drift items are `complete`. The raw comparison omits the locked-row merge, which can only turn a mismatch INTO agreement, so a raw zero implies a merged zero.
